The ratio of silicon atoms in the photospheres of Star_1 and Star_2 is determined by their abundances relative to hydrogen. Using the given bracket notation:

For Star_1:
- [Fe/H]_1 = 0 dex → (Fe/H)_1 = (Fe/H)_Sun
- [Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3 dex → (Si/Fe)_1 = 10^0.3 × (Si/Fe)_Sun
Thus, (Si/H)_1 = (Si/Fe)_1 × (Fe/H)_1 = 10^0.3 × (Si/H)_Sun.

For Star_2:
- [Mg/H]_2 = 0 dex → (Mg/H)_2 = (Mg/H)_Sun
- [Mg/Si]_2 = 0.3 dex → (Mg/Si)_2 = 10^0.3 × (Mg/Si)_Sun → (Si/Mg)_2 = 10^{-0.3} × (Si/Mg)_Sun
Thus, (Si/H)_2 = (Si/Mg)_2 × (Mg/H)_2 = 10^{-0.3} × (Si/H)_Sun.

The ratio of silicon atoms (number densities) is:
(Si/H)_1 / (Si/H)_2 = 10^0.3 / 10^{-0.3} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98.

This matches option (D). The stellar masses are extraneous information.

Answer: D
